oscar: 4 Oscars! Music, sound, and visual effects
story: A lonely boy named Elliott finds a gentle alien hiding behind his house, left behind when his spaceship had to blast off without him. Elliott and his brother and sister hide E.T. from the grown-ups and help him build a machine to phone home. But the longer E.T. stays on Earth, the weaker he gets, and government agents are closing in.
trivia_title: E.T. phone home! Did you know...
trivia: Elliott lures E.T. with a trail of Reese's Pieces. After the movie came out, sales of the candy went through the roof.
E.T.'s croaky voice was mostly performed by Pat Welsh, a California grandma with a wonderfully raspy voice.
E.T.'s face was designed from three real faces: the poet Carl Sandburg, Albert Einstein and Ernest Hemingway.
Spielberg shot the movie in order from start to finish, so when the kids say goodbye to E.T., the tears are real.

scenes: Elliott, Gertie and Michael. Watch their faces every time E.T. does something new.
Gertie's flowers. They droop and bloom to tell you how E.T. is feeling before anyone says a word.
The glowing finger heals. Count how many times you see it light up.
questions: At the start, Elliott is lonely and nobody listens to him. By the end, he is the bravest kid in town. What changed him?
Spielberg filmed almost the whole movie from a kid's eye height, looking up at the grown-up world. Why would he do that?
E.T. loves Elliott, but he still chooses to go home. Was that the right ending? What would you have chosen?
